That is the market's actual structure; it is an objective-only cap with no LP structural change (emissions and heat rate stay on the gas characterization), it adds ZERO free parameters, and it is costless at every scored grain. miso-121's own matrix note flagged exactly this as 'an OWNER call, not a session call'; the owner made it. Per miso-122's DO-NOT-MISREAD the max class-hour delta is NOT the magnitude at MISO; the magnitude is per-class ENERGY, and 2024's is CC_REGULAR -0.337 GWh / CT_PEAKER +0.318 GWh / ST_CHP +0.063 / ST_GAS -0.026 / CC_CHP -0.016 / oil -0.002 GWh, with 2023 identically zero and 2025 ~0.02 GWh -- of order 0.0003 TWh against a MISO load in the hundreds of TWh, the same ~0.002 %-of-energy scale miso-121 measured. THIS KEEPER'S OWN DELTA (miso-124): MISO's oil/gas switch-capable fleet is now priced the way the market prices it -- a unit flagged Multifuel on EIA-860 burns whichever fuel is cheaper, so its delivered price is min(gas, oil). The cap reaches 371 / 371 / 369 gas tranches (15,827 / 15,827 / 15,825 MW = 23.3 % of MISO gas) in 2023 / 2024 / 2025, with the parity price taken from 12/12 measured MISO F923 Petroleum months in every year (20.36 / 18.22 / 17.21 $/MMBtu -- the flat national fallback is never reached). ZERO free parameters: both legs are published measured registries and the mechanism is the arithmetic min() of them, with no coefficient between. It is INERT at every scored grain and that is the expected, measured result, not a failure: CAMPD's own meters put observed MISO dual-fuel oil generation at ~0.002 % of ISO energy, so the real phenomenon is too small to move an ISO-level annual criterion. Every criterion verdict, the determination and the ledgered caveats are IDENTICAL to the predecessor 2026-08-04-miso-122b-scope-gate; the whole price effect is 6 hours of mid-January 2024 (max zonal |dLMP| 1.383 $/MWh, system demand-weighted -0.000159), one-sided downward as a min() cap requires, and ~0.0003 TWh of class energy. Armed on rule 1 [R-STRUCT] structural fidelity under an explicit owner call, restoring an arming that miso-121 established and a merge race dropped.

THIS KEEPER'S OWN DELTA (miso-122): MISO's topping-cycle CHP plants are priced on a heat rate that no longer charges direct-fired host-process fuel to their power tranches. eGRID publishes ONE CHP heat-input split per PLANT, which cannot see a HYBRID cogen -- a topping CC/CT train plus a package boiler on the same ORIS code -- so plant 55088 Dearborn passed the derive's 0.50 unfired-topping ceiling on a plant-average thermal_share of 0.2396 while 16.6 % of its metered fuel burned in three 'Other boiler' units reporting ZERO gross load all year. CAMPD/CEMS resolves that at UNIT grain, and the derive now removes it: heat_rate = (PLHTIAN + CHPCHTI) * (1 - dark_fuel_share) / PLNGENAN. A SHARE, never an MMBtu subtraction, so it needs CEMS's fuel COMPOSITION to be representative and never CEMS's LEVEL to equal eGRID's; the denominator is unchanged, zero free parameters, no threshold, byte no-op wherever no dark fuel exists. Applied to 3 (plant, class) rows: 55088 CC_CHP (350 MW) and CT_CHP (165 MW) 8.3465 -> 6.9573 (-16.6 %), 10745 Midland Cogeneration Venture (1,479 MW) 8.8243 -> 8.8160 (-0.09 %). Against a byte-identical same-HEAD control: CC_CHP +0.3575/+0.2718/+0.5190 TWh and CT_CHP +0.2197/+0.2218/+0.2240 TWh, displacing CC_REGULAR, imports and COAL_PRB -- the correctly-priced cogen now runs where it should -- at max zonal |dLMP| 0.0491/0.0390/0.0752 $/MWh, under the 0.10 pre-registered bar in all three years. Every criterion verdict is UNCHANGED (12/12 free, 16/16 all, the same single C7 COAL_PRB shape FAIL). Promoted on structural fidelity under rules 1 [R-STRUCT] / 14 [R-ACCURATE], never on a score, and it also closes a reproducibility seam: the predecessor keeper solved on the pre-gate artifact and stopped being reproducible from HEAD once the corrected input landed. Two dark-fuel plants outside MISO (NYISO 2493 East River, NEISO 1595 Kendall) are handed to their own lanes -- no parameter crosses an ISO boundary (rule 25).
